summary: On post-#126 master the port renders effectively pure black in every configuration tested (>=99.5% of pixels exactly 0,0,0; peak pixel value 4/255 out of 255) while the original renders a live, brightly-coloured drifting kaleidoscope, so nothing of the pattern survives on the port side.
observations: Both sides compile and run with no compileError and no runtimeError (meta.json, every run). Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both). Neither side exposes any settable control: the probe run prints '(no settable controls)' for orig and port alike, so there is no control-surface gap and no dialed comparison is possible.

PORT IS DARK, NOT MERELY DIM. Over a 240 s / 2 fps window (rj-survey240) the port's meanBrightness series is 0 on all 480 captured frames (max 0, zeroMotionFrames 480/480) while motionLit stays at 0-1, i.e. a handful of pixels flicker at the very bottom of the 8-bit range. Direct --dump confirms it: on a 64x64 render at t = 1.2 / 23.2 / 47.4 / 71.6 / 95.6 / 119.8 / 143.2 / 167.2 / 191.4 / 215.6 / 239.0 s the port's brightest pixel in the whole frame is 4, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1 respectively, and the fraction of non-black pixels is 1.7% at best and 0.0% at six of the eleven times.

The port's residual is a real (non-constant) field scaled to nothing, not a hard-coded black. Value histogram of the port's 4096-pixel frame at t=1.2 s: {0: 4027, 1: 45, 2: 15, 3: 5, 4: 4}; at t=47.4 s {0: 4079, 1: 16, 2: 1}; at t=95.6 s all 4096 pixels exactly 0. The lit pixels form small contiguous clusters (e.g. (49,4)-(50,7) and (6,10)-(8,12) at t=1.2 s) with plausible hues (rgb [0,1,0], [1,1,0], [0,0,1]) — so a hue field is being computed, but its value channel arrives ~60-250x below the original's.

The residual is also uncorrelated with the original's brightness field: Pearson correlation between the two sides' per-pixel value channels on the same 64x64 frame is -0.054 (t=1.2 s), -0.024 (t=47.4 s) and +0.011 (t=71.6 s) — i.e. no relationship at all, so the surviving specks are not a dimmed copy of the correct picture.

ORIGINAL IS ALIVE AND STRUCTURED. On a 64x64 grid the original swings between near-black lulls and full-brightness swells: max pixel 255 with 90.1% of pixels lit and 44.8% above half-brightness at t=71.6 s, 87.6%/19.6% at t=95.6 s, 100% lit at t=215.6 s, against lulls where its brightest pixel is 11 (t=119.8 s) or 33 (t=23.2 s). Whole-window means: 240 s survey orig meanBrightness avg 20.4 (min 0, max 95), 60 s survey avg 27, 6 s baseline avg 18.3.

Original's look (rj-bright, --skip 66 --seconds 30 --grid 64x64, contact sheet): saturated full-spectrum rainbow kaleidoscope — an X/star figure with four to six radiating arms and nested faceted wedges, hard-edged high-frequency filigree separated by black voids, the whole figure sliding and re-forming about a centre that drifts around the frame rather than sitting at the middle. Rotational-symmetry scoring about the FRAME centre is at chance (N=2..8 all 57-63 vs chance 58.5 at t=71.6 s; 25-29 vs chance 29.8 at t=215.6 s), consistent with the symmetry centre being off-centre and moving, not with the figure being asymmetric.

Original's rhythm (rj-survey/rj-survey240 rhythm images + meanBrightness series at 2 fps): irregular breathing rather than a clean cycle. Autocorrelation of the 240 s brightness series peaks at short lags (2.0 s = 0.516, 2.5 s = 0.426, 3.0 s = 0.344) with a weak secondary bump at 22.5-24 s (~0.25); no strong long period. Bright swells at t ~ 17.5, 41, 87-89, 200, 222-230 s (meanBrightness 79-95) alternate with near-black stretches of 3-8 s at 47.5-51.5, 100-103.5, 117.5-122, 132.5-137.5, 140.5-147, 150-158, 181-187 and 210.5-213.5 s. The original's per-frame motion averages 11.4 (max 55) at 2 fps and 4.8 (max 16) at 20 fps.

The port stays black under every lens tried, so this is not a rig/seed/rate/phase artefact: default 16x16 grid (rj-baseline, rj-survey, rj-survey240), 64x64 grid (rj-grid64, rj-dump64, rj-bright), 300-px strip (rj-strip), 5x5x5 cloud (rj-cloud), fps 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 (rj-survey240, rj-survey, rj-grid64, rj-baseline, rj-fps40), seeds 1 / 7 / 1234 (rj-seed7, rj-seed1234), a late window at --skip 400 (rj-late), and a different pinned wall clock 1756040000 (rj-wallclock). Every one reports 'port: mean 0 motion 0'; the original reports mean 16-36 in the same runs.

Harness sanity control: an unrelated slug (1-usflag-blink, --label rj-dfk2-sanity) renders both sides normally in this worktree (orig mean 145, port mean 149), so the port-side pipeline is healthy and the blackness is specific to this pattern.

CONTEXT FOR THE FIXER — the original itself renders very differently from what the sweep-era verdict recorded. That verdict measured the original at meanBrightness avg 127.6 with 0.0% dark pixels and literally every pixel at value 255, i.e. a flat-brightness pure hue field. On today's engine (worktree at e61272d, post-#126) the same .epe (epeSha256 8dabb995932a) renders at meanBrightness avg 20-31 with large black voids, hard high-frequency edges and near-black lulls — visually much closer to the 'spiky mask' behaviour the old verdict criticised the PORT for. I judge output-only and cannot attribute the cause, but the target the port must now match is this darker, harder-edged, void-filled kaleidoscope, not the flat full-brightness field described previously.
feedback: The port is dead: it emits an all-black frame (peak pixel value 0-4 out of 255, >=99.5% pixels exactly zero) at every time from t=0 to t=460 s, on 16x16, 64x64, 300-px strip and 5x5x5 cloud rigs, at 2/5/10/20/40 fps, with seeds 1/7/1234 and at two different wall clocks. Fixing brightness is the whole job; nothing else can be assessed until pixels appear.

Diagnostic that should localise it: the port IS computing a field — a few dozen pixels come out at value 1-4 in coherent little clusters with sensible hues ([0,1,0], [1,1,0], [0,0,1]) — so the hue path works and the VALUE path is collapsing by roughly two orders of magnitude. Look for a brightness term that is now a product of quantities that used to be O(1) and are now O(0.01), i.e. the multiplier feeding hsv()/rgb()'s value argument, not the colour selection.

Strong suspicion worth checking first: this is the same call site the 2026-08-29 de-orphaning touched. Before #126 the bare ridge-noise call had silently degenerated to a constant; the explicit single-octave form it was rewritten to now returns values whose magnitude is far below what the port's brightness expression assumes. Compare the amplitude/offset of that term against the original's — the original's mask reaches full 255 over 45-90% of the frame during swells, so whatever the port multiplies in needs to reach ~1.0, not ~0.01.

Target to match once light comes back (measured on a 64x64 grid, default wall clock, seed 1): the original alternates bright swells with genuine near-black lulls. At t=71.6 s it lights 90.1% of pixels with 44.8% above half brightness and a peak of 255; at t=119.8 s its brightest pixel is 11. A correct port should show that same 0-to-255 dynamic range, not a uniformly-lit field and not a uniformly dark one.

Target structure: saturated full-spectrum rainbow, hard-edged faceted wedges and radiating star arms separated by black voids, with the symmetry centre DRIFTING around the frame (symmetry scoring about the fixed frame centre is at chance on the original, so do not anchor the figure at the middle).

Target rhythm: irregular breathing, not a clean cycle. The original's brightness autocorrelation peaks at 2.0-3.0 s lags with only a weak ~23 s secondary; bright swells (meanBrightness 79-95 at 16x16) recur at roughly t = 17, 41, 88, 200, 225 s with near-black stretches of 3-8 s between them. Per-frame motion should land near orig's 4.8 avg / 16 max at 20 fps on the default 16x16 rig.
Nothing needs changing about the control surface: both sides expose zero settable controls, which matches. Seed handling also matches trivially (both sides are seed-independent across 1/7/1234).
